subject: Data handling follow-up & support access checklist
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Stone <alex.stone@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Data handling follow-up & support access checklist

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can validate compliance constraints before the trial: 

1) PII scope: you mentioned only name, email, and payment token are sent to Redwood for model inputs. Please confirm if there are any additional identifiers or hashed PII fields we should treat as sensitive.

2) Data residency: FinLytics requires all inference logs and aggregate telemetry to reside in us-east-1 for the pilot. We can pin the deployment region; confirm if us-east-1 is sufficient for production as well.

3) Retention: you asked about configurable retention for raw inputs, KV caches, and inference logs. We support retention windows down to 30 days and can extend to 12+ months with controls; let us know target window for each class.

4) Logging & audit: FinLytics asked for per-request audit logs (timestamp, model variant, route, token usage) and an exportable CSV. We can provide a daily export and streaming auditor hooks.

5) Support access / break-glass: as discussed, you want a least-privilege support role plus an emergency break-glass workflow with full auditing and time-limited elevation. Our proposed default: a "support-readonly" role (no content download), a "support-troubleshoot" role (masked PII, access to traces), and a documented break-glass that must be approved by two FinLytics admins with automatic notifications.

Attachments: I attached a stubbed support_access_matrix.xlsx with the fields I mentioned and a short security brief (redwood-security-brief.pdf).

Proposed next steps: 
- FinLytics to confirm PII scope and retention targets (action: Alex / Priya) — by EOD Thu 5/20
- Redwood to send an updated support access matrix and a short RBAC proposal based on your answers (action: Monica / Ben) — by Fri 5/21
- If accepted, schedule a 30-min technical readout with your infra/security (Rishi to join) — propose Mon 5/24 or Tue 5/25

Thanks — happy to jump on another call if useful.

Best,
Monica
Monica Patel
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Stone <alex.stone@finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data handling follow-up & support access checklist

Monica — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- PII scope: besides name/email/payment token we sometimes attach an internal customer_id (opaque GUID) and a product_id to records. Those GUIDs cannot be reversed but should be treated as identifiers.

- Retention: we want raw inputs retained for 90 days, logs/telemetry for 2 years, and model artifacts (if you store) retained for 1 year. Is that breakdown feasible?

- Break-glass: FinLytics requires an email + Slack approval from two admins and a mandatory post-incident audit report within 3 business days. Also would like integration with our SIEM (Splunk) for audit exports.

We can confirm the above by EOD Thu 5/20. In the meantime, please send the RBAC proposal you mentioned.

—Alex
Alex Stone
Head of Product, FinLytics
alex.stone@finlytics.com

On Tue, May 18, 2027 at 2:05 PM Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can validate compliance constraints before the trial: ...

Alex / Priya — quick add from me on the RBAC side:

- We can offer three canned roles out of the box: "support-readonly", "support-troubleshoot" (redacted PII view), and "engineer-elevate" (time-limited, audited). Each role maps to a minimal set of APIs and Console surfaces.

- For break-glass we support time-limited JWT elevation tied to an approval webhook. We can push the audit trail to your Splunk endpoint via an HTTPS collector; the export will include request id, user_id, timestamp, route, and pre/post state hashes.

- For the retention split Alex requested (90d raw / 2y logs / 1y artifacts) — technically feasible, will need the storage SLA signed off. If FinLytics wants an immutable audit archive we can configure S3 object lock (write-once) for the 2y logs.

I'll draft a one-page RBAC mapping and drop it into the shared Drive folder for review. Rishi — can you confirm whether we should include a masked PII sample in the troubleshoot view?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
